newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London stocks scale new peaks, dollar weaker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London stocks scale new peaks, dollar weaker.

text.p: London stocks scaled yet more peaks on Friday afternoon, lifted further by Wall Street which surged ahead at the start on Friday as fears receded of higher U.S. interest rates.

But on currency markets, the interest rate expectations had the opposite effect, driving the dollar down sharply against the yen and mark as dollar-denominated assets became less attractive to investors.
The London bourse's sparkling performance began when stocks hit a trading peak in the morning session, then roared ahead further after lunch when New York opened and made rapid gains.

The rest of Europe, meanwhile, was having a lacklustre day. The strong Wall Street opening helped Paris to cut its losses but Frankfurt floor trade, which ended before New York started, finished with only modest gains.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, climbed by one percent to 4,629.0 points within an hour of opening, overtaking Thursday's record close of 4,580.4, itself the fifth consecutive closing high.

But investors pushed it to a new high of 4643.4 as New York's Dow Jones industrials shot up by 0.7 percent on the strength of overnight comments by U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan quelling prospects of near-term interest rate hikes.

London's six-day bull run, with records tumbling almost daily, has been fuelled by investors' optimism over the new Labour government's decision to give the central bank more freedom in setting interest rates.
The pace picked up on Friday even before Wall Street's injection of adrenalin as talk of bids in the banking sector caused a shortage of stocks, forcing up prices.
"It's all got a bit squeezy... fundamentally with low inflation and reasonable growth people are starting to believe that Labour will deliver," said NatWest strategist, Bob Semple.
"It's an amazing market today," said one dealer.
Barclays climbed 65p to 1274p and the Royal Bank of
Scotland surged by 60p to 662p as the outbreak of bid speculation increased demand in a sector that has risen sharply this year.

The strength in Wall Street, however, failed to do much for continental Europe. Deals on Frankfurt's computerised IBIS index were barely in the plus column, perhaps depressed by the weaker dollar which was seen as harming exports.
And Frankfurt floor trade ended ahead a few points after thin trading with many investors having extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend.

Paris shares had a bad day, slipping in and out of profit in weak volumes in reaction to the falling dollar and an opinion poll giving the centre-right just a thin majority ahead of the May 25/June 1 election.
French shares cut their losses somewhat after Wall Street opened higher but were still showing a loss of 0.3 percent by midafternoon.
In currencies, the dollar sank by over a pfennig and two yen in thin transactions as the U.S. currency was hurt by increasingly divergent rate expectations for Japan and the United States.

Greenspan's overnight comments were seen by many as reducing the chances of higher U.S. interest rates. At the same time, Japanese officials continued their verbal support for the yen and speculation also grew of a Japanese rate rise.
"Greenspan wasn't suggesting there was likely to be any more (rate tightening) very soon...On that basis the dollar's easier," said Adrian Schmidt, international economist at Chase here.
Traders said volume was extremely thin, amplifying exchange rate moves, as many continental European traders had extended Thursday's Ascension Day holiday into a long weekend.

The yen drew support from a Japanese press report which speculated on the chances of a discount rate rise there in July. Some in the Bank of Japan think its low interest rate policy should end soon, the Nikkei Kinyu story suggested.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka expressed the hope that markets would "further digest" the G7 accord reached in April, when the group agreed to monitor foreign exchange developments and cooperate as appropriate in the markets.
"It's clear Japanese officials are continuing to try to talk down the dollar," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
STOCK PRICES AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 59.3 points at 4,639.7.
The Paris CAC-40 index down 10.50 points to 2,632.81.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 10.43 points at 3,562.41.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6937 marks compared with 1.7073 late in Europe on Thursday and 121.66 yen versus 123.76.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $345.85 after closing at $343.90 an ounce in London on Thursday. Silver was $4.83 down one cent.
